description: PROMOTED — the at-least-once receiver contract (SPEC section 7.1). Both registered wire shapes ride HTTP, which is at-least-once: a push whose ack is lost is retried by a CORRECT client, so the same message arrives twice by design, not only on bad networks. Behaviour, not bytes, so it is pinned as a decision table. Promoted 2026-07-26: implemented independently by two teams (2026-07-22) and then exercised across a full six-sub-game cross-team series over public tunnels on 2026-07-25, mutual audits clean both ways.

state_shape.played: {step: commit} — every step already applied, keyed by the commit that sealed it
state_shape.window: how many out-of-order steps may be buffered; 0 means none
state_shape.next: the next step this receiver expects to apply

arrivals.note: redelivery: SAME commit for a played step -> absorb, state unchanged. Dedupe on the commit, not on (kind, step)
a DIFFERENT commit for a played step -> equivocation. This is tampering evidence and must stay loud; a (kind, step) key would have collapsed it silently into the row above
one ahead, inside the reorder window -> buffer and replay in step order
at the window bound -> still buffered
past the window -> violation. Let the window BE the flood rule; a second threshold beside it is unreachable

below `next` and never played -> discard. `next` only advances past accepted steps, so this can never become applicable; buffering it holds it forever and two conformant receivers could diverge on it. NOTE: this row postdates the 2026-07-25/08-04 promotions and is not yet reproduced by a second implementation (anrbj666's audit, 2026-08-04)

no_reorder_window.note: the same one-ahead arrival against a receiver with window=0. A receiver with no reorder window turns an ordinary retry race into a protocol violation — under App. E rule 35 that is a self-inflicted technical loss zeroing BOTH teams. Zero tolerance is not a tightening here.

deadline_rule.note: tolerated traffic arrived -> the deadline does NOT move: one clock per EXPECTED message, so a stall burns the sender's budget, not ours
expires on a lap where a message DID arrive — a receiver that checks its clock only on an empty poll never checks it under a flood

no_rules_tolerance: none of this relaxes commit-reveal. Transport tolerance, no rules tolerance: equivocation still collapses the game.
